title: Voice input and text selection
summary: Set up recognition channels, a microphone and shortcuts to dictate into your input field.
body:
Get one speech channel working first

  1. Open Voice input and add a supported account source, or configure a separate speech-recognition API model. An ordinary chat model does not necessarily support speech recognition.
  2. Check the speech API URL, model and authorization. You can configure up to three different channels: the first is primary and the others are backups. Drag them to change their order.
  3. Select the default microphone or a specific device, run the test, and check that the level changes as you speak. Stop the test when you finish.
  4. Try recognizing a short sentence first. Once the text looks right, set a shortcut that does not conflict with your usual software.

Use it in the input field where you are working

  1. First place the cursor in a chat box, editor or another text input field.
  2. Start recording with the microphone control or a shortcut. Shortcuts support both hold-to-talk and toggle modes.
  3. After you stop recording, wait for recognition and insertion to finish. Check the inserted text before deciding whether to send it.
  4. If focus changes or the system prevents insertion, copy the retained transcription and paste it manually. You can also replay the recording when needed.

What the Voice Island shows

The Voice Island shows recording, recognition, insertion and completion states. Adjust its theme, colors and size to suit your desktop. It serves a different purpose from the Usage Island: the Voice Island follows the input process, while the Usage Island shows account and model usage.

Translate or ask about selected text

Configure an available text model first, then enable selection translation or questions. After selecting text, start an action near the selection and choose the target translation language. Each selection is limited to 16,000 characters; split longer text into sections.

If the system cannot retrieve the selection, copy it first and use Paste and translate. The original text is retained if an attempt fails, so you can retry. Without a configured text model, a translation will not appear automatically.

No sound, an inactive shortcut or failed text insertion

  • No microphone level: check the selected device, system input volume and microphone permissions first.
  • Shortcut not working: check for key conflicts and system keyboard-monitoring permissions. Text insertion on macOS may also require Accessibility permission.
  • Linux / Wayland: shortcuts, text selection and insertion depend on your desktop’s portal or bridge support. Configure them for your actual environment.
  • Recognition request failed: check the channel’s service type, URL, credentials and network connection. A remote speech API does not provide fully offline recognition.

A useful combination

Place the cursor in the AI Assistant input field, dictate the full task, and check the transcription before sending it. When reading material in another language, translate a selection first, then give the assistant a request you understand. Voice input reduces typing; reviewing the text before sending still helps prevent recognition errors from changing your intent.

title: Usage Island
summary: Keep usage on your desktop and choose from five layouts to suit the way you work.
body:
What information belongs on your desktop

The Usage Island puts remaining account quotas, reset countdowns or API model balances into a small floating desktop window. Glance at it while working instead of repeatedly returning to a management page. It displays status; it does not increase quotas or automatically switch accounts for every tool.

First-time setup

  1. Open Usage Island at the top of App Desktop. Prepare available sources in Account Center or Model Center first.
  2. Choose the accounts or models to display, up to six. Start with the sources you use most or whose quotas run out most easily.
  3. Choose a layout and expansion direction, then select hover, click-to-expand or always-open behavior.
  4. Adjust the theme, size and opacity for your desktop background, then enable the Usage Island.
  5. Refresh manually when you need new data, or choose a refresh interval that suits your needs.

Choosing among the five layouts

LayoutWhere it fitsExpansion direction
HorizontalAlong a screen edge or in a wider open areaLeft / Right
VerticalIn a narrow area at the sideUp / Down
DialA compact view of several sourcesClockwise / Counterclockwise
ListFor reading each status individuallyInformation arranged as a list
LinesA horizontal overview with a small footprintExpands in the selected direction

Layout and direction change presentation only. They do not change account permissions, model capabilities or routing priority.

Theme, size, opacity and refresh

Themes include the theme color, dark, light and system-following options. Size ranges from 70% to 150%, and opacity from 20% to 100%. If the text is too small, increase the size first, then adjust its position.

Refresh is manual by default. You can also choose 5, 15, 30 or 60 minutes. Whether a source supports refreshing, and which fields it provides, depends on that integration. An unknown value must not be treated as a zero balance.

Enable Smart Routes status to observe current access activity. This is a status display, not an additional route.

Use it with Smart Routes

Set up your everyday access configuration first, then add your usual accounts or models to the Usage Island. When a quota is nearly exhausted, return to the relevant page to refresh and check it before changing sources or priorities. The Usage Island flags states that need attention; actual account and model application remains on the corresponding management pages.

title: Pets and TokenPet
summary: Turn tokens recorded through Smart Routes into pet growth, and learn about hatching, leveling up and supplies.
body:
Start with a pet

Open Pets at the top of App Desktop. Six voxel pets are currently available in different colors: Iron Bean, Rainbow unicorn, Spined kaiju, Nine-tailed fox, Alien and Mr. Kangaroo. Select a pet, drag to rotate it, or adjust the viewing angle with the arrow keys.

TokenPet is a growth unit within the pet system. It is not an API balance, cannot be cashed out, and does not add usable quota with a provider.

Where TokenPet comes from

The system uses cumulative token consumption recorded in the Smart Routes ledger and credits only the increase to your pet growth balance, preventing the same cumulative usage from being credited twice. Enable Record statistics in Settings, and make sure upstream responses provide recognizable usage data.

Only recorded access usage counts

Consumption across all your websites, third-party tools and accounts is not automatically monitored or converted. Usage that does not pass through Smart Routes, or has no corresponding usable record, may not generate TokenPet. You do not need to spend extra model tokens to complete the beginner tutorial.

How to hatch and level up

  1. Check your TokenPet balance and select the pet you want to raise.
  2. Click Level up to put the available balance toward growth. If it is not enough for a full level, experience can accumulate within the current level.
  3. Wait for leveling and stage animations to finish before taking the next action. Watch the pet progress from an egg and cracked shell to a baby and adult.
  4. To raise more pets, buy a new egg at the price shown on the page. An egg currently costs 100 million TokenPet; use the displayed price and upgrade cost as your reference.

Growth stages

LevelForm
0–9Whole egg
10–19Cracked egg
20–29Baby
30–49Young
50–60Adult; the current maximum level is 60

What pet supplies do

  • Growth card:Adds TokenPet within the pet system.
  • Double card:Affects growth-card rewards for 15 minutes at present; it does not double model quota.
  • Haste card:Brings the next supply forward. It does not speed up model inference.

Check the page’s countdown for eligibility and the next supply time. Pets provide companionship alongside your work; they are not a prerequisite for using applications, models or Smart Routes.

title: Plugins
summary: Discover and manage extensions, including installation sources, permissions and updates.
body:
What plugins add

The Plugins page at the top of App Desktop lets you discover and manage extensions. Plugins can provide application entries, account integrations, appearance options or other features. Installing one is different from installing a third-party AI client: the client is the tool you use, while a plugin adds supported capabilities within EchoBird.

Find an extension in the catalog

  1. Open Plugins and browse the catalog or installed items for the extension you need.
  2. Narrow the results with search or categories such as apps, accounts, appearance and features.
  3. Switch between international, domestic or CNB sources when needed. If refreshing fails, check the selected source first. The installed list and online catalog are separate sets of data.
  4. Select an extension and review its name, description, source, version and permissions on the right, then use the installation action provided.

Add from a repository or local directory

The Add menu offers repository and local-directory options. Use a URL or extension directory whose source you have verified. Wait for the candidate extension’s information to be parsed, then read its permissions and complete installation. Not every folder is a valid plugin.

Account plugins involve authorized access, and model-request permission may let a plugin use models. Clipboard, configuration, storage, command and background capabilities each have their own purposes too. Check permissions against the features you intend to use rather than installing based only on a similar name.

Enable, update and uninstall

After installation, enable and use the plugin through the controls it provides. You can check for updates on the right. If an update adds permissions, confirmation is required again; canceling that confirmation does not complete the update.

Uninstallation requires confirmation. Removing an extension may make its account capabilities or interface entries unavailable. Remaining cached content does not mean the service can still perform operations. If an update fails, check the source, network connection and specific error before retrying.

The account service you want is missing

Check whether the service is provided through an account plugin and whether that plugin is installed and enabled. Then return to Account Center or the relevant tool page. Plugins can add integration methods, but cannot bypass provider login, permissions or subscription restrictions.

title: AI Latest News
summary: Read news by date in one place and open the original article when needed.
body:
Read news for a selected date

  1. Open AI Latest News from the sidebar and wait for the content to load.
  2. The Simplified Chinese interface can switch between domestic and global sources. Other interface languages use global sources.
  3. Select a date in the date tree on the right. The list shows content for that date.
  4. Review titles, sources and relative timestamps, then click an item to open the original article.

Refreshing and cached history

Use Refresh when you want new content. Existing cached items are retained if the network fails, so there is no need to clear your history or reinstall just to reload. When looking at older content, also check the current source and date before assuming that all historical data is gone.

Keep reading separate from execution

AI Latest News brings news together; the original content and opinions come from the respective sources. If you discover a new tool, check whether it is listed in App Desktop. Before trying it, review its actual system requirements and official instructions. Reading news does not automatically install tools or make the assistant execute commands from an article.

If you do not need the news entry, disable AI Latest News in Settings to keep the sidebar simpler.

title: My AI Career
summary: Review local sessions and activity patterns, and find work you can continue.
body:
What the overview shows

My AI Career organizes local sessions and activity records from supported tools. The overview includes session count, message count, approximate cumulative tokens, active days and longest streak, with a contribution heatmap and daily activity chart to show your usage patterns.

Available fields vary by tool. Token counts include estimates and should not be treated as a provider bill. Missing records do not necessarily mean you have never used a tool.

Find a previous session

  1. Open My AI Career, wait for local records to load, and begin by reviewing activity by date.
  2. Select a tool family to view its session list.
  3. Find the session you need and check its timestamp, content summary and available project path or session information.
  4. Use the actions available for that tool to copy the session ID, resume command or project path, or locate the record file.
  5. Return to the corresponding tool to continue working. Resume capabilities are not identical across all tools and sessions.

How it fits with other pages

App Desktop helps you open tools; My AI Career helps you review your activity in them. To resume work, find the session and project path first, then check the account and model source in App Desktop. This can reduce the need to explain the context again from scratch.

This page focuses on local sessions and activity records, rather than a shared team task board. A project path is information associated with a session; copying it does not automatically migrate or back up the entire project.
